## F — Parking, backing and freeway driving
Research index: 29 original C facts and 20 continuation or confusable C2 facts cover Parking, backing and freeway driving.
Exam index: part A cites cover edition, publisher frontmatter and the physical testing page; no passing percentage or time limit is asserted.
VERIFY: ID-FREEWAY-PERCENT — official percentage not printed; ID-FREEWAY-TIME — official time limit unlocated; ID-FREEWAY-EFFECTIVE — effective date unestablished.
VERIFY: ID-FREEWAY-DYNAMIC — Actual speed postings, weather, reserved-parking eligibility and installed controls require their current official context; no location-specific permission is invented.
VERIFY: ID-FREEWAY-MARKET — demand research missing; ID-FREEWAY-COMPETITORS — competitor research missing.
Every open item stays assigned to the evidence or research owner in its originating chunk. Pedagogic priorities are not official topic weights.
VERIFY: ID-HILL-PARKING-VISUAL — Physical page eighty-one includes hill-parking illustrations. Text supports the wheel-turn directions below, but wheel contact and any rolling sequence shown in the image have not been visually reviewed; no sequence is inferred from the phrase away and against the curb.
VERIFY: ID-RESERVED-PARKING-SYMBOL — The disability-parking symbol on physical page eighty-two is image content not semantically reviewed. Textual eligibility and reserved-space use are covered; visual recognition remains unresolved.
VERIFY: ID-FREEWAY-SHORT-RAMP-SPAN — The instruction to wait for a sufficiently large gap after stopping on a short acceleration lane spans physical pages eighty-four and eighty-five. The current one-page fact binding cannot represent that complete conditional instruction without losing its interference qualifier; retain the complete span as coverage debt.
VERIFY: ID-FREEWAY-CROSSOVER-USERS — Physical page eighty-four names highway-maintenance or emergency vehicles as crossover users, while physical page eighty-five says emergency vehicles only. Ordinary-driver prohibition is supported by both; the authorized-user distinction needs issuer reconciliation.
VERIFY: ID-RESERVED-PARKING-PRIVILEGES — The handbook describes no-payment and unlimited-time use by a person with a disability in symbol-designated reserved parking. Do not generalize that statement to other spaces, private facilities or present local meter policies without their official evidence.
